entry.name: OSMO
entry.title: OSMO: Open-Source Tactile Glove for Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer
entry.summary: Open-source glove with 12 three-axis magnetic taxels on fingertips and palm; ~2 h of right-hand whiteboard-wiping demonstrations with a static RealSense D435 (RGB + IR stereo), of which one 8.4 s sample is released.
entry.hand: human right hand wearing the OSMO glove (the same glove is worn by a Psyonic Ability Hand at robot deployment)

sensor.note: 12 three-axis taxels: one per fingertip plus palm sensors in three sections. Each sensor PCB has two Bosch BMM350 3-axis magnetometers and one Bosch BHI360 6-axis IMU, under a soft magnetic elastomer (Ecoflex 00-30 + Magnequench MQFP-15-7) with a MuMetal shield; the two readings per taxel are used differentially. Raw magnetic flux (stated as uT) is the tactile signal. The paper policy and the released sample use only the 5 fingertip taxels: one sample = 30 values (5 fingertips x 2 magnetometers x XYZ).
sensor.maker: custom (Meta FAIR); DIY kit sold by WowRobo

scale.text: ~2 h, 140 human wiping demonstrations (paper); released: 1 sample demonstration, 211 frames, 8.4 s

entry.access: One sample demonstration (folder "00", four Python pickles, 972 MB) on a public Google Drive folder linked from the repository's data/README.md (2025-12-21); the 140-demonstration set is not released, and data/download_data.sh is still empty. Hardware, firmware and code are in the GitHub repository.
caveats: Only one 8.4 s sample demonstration is released; the paper's 140 demonstrations (~2 h) are not.
No license for the data or the repository: no LICENSE file, and the ROS package metadata says 'TODO: License declaration'.
Released tactile data covers the 5 fingertip taxels only (30 values per frame); palm taxels and the per-sensor IMU quaternions are not in the release.
No hand pose, depth or retargeted robot joints are released; they are produced by the repository's pipeline (SAM2 + HaMeR, FoundationStereo on the IR pair, mink IK).
The IR images are masked to a region of interest with white pixels (about 62-65% of each frame) for demonstrator privacy; the RGB images are not masked.
Data are Python pickles; the image files need numpy to unpickle, so load them with a restricted unpickler.
RGB frames are stored in BGR channel order (OpenCV bgr8).
Hand-tracking compatibility demos (Aria Gen 2, Quest 3, Apple Vision Pro, RGB video, Manus Quantum) appear on the project page but are not released as data.
No robot data is recorded; the robot (Franka + Psyonic Ability Hand wearing the glove) is used only for policy deployment.

cameras.note: single scene camera, extrinsically calibrated to the robot base; same placement used at robot deployment. Stream configured at 1280x720 bgr8 30 fps and published to ROS2 every 0.04 s (25 Hz).

cameras.model: Intel RealSense D435 (IR pair, same unit)
cameras.note: left/right IR images (mono8), IR emitter disabled in the capture node; masked to a region of interest with white fill in the release; used offline for FoundationStereo depth

tracking.note: 3-D keypoints and hand mesh estimated from the RGB images after recording; not in the release

tracking.system: HaMeR wrist refined with FoundationStereo depth from the IR pair
tracking.note: Savitzky-Golay smoothed, then IK-retargeted (mink/MuJoCo) to Franka + Psyonic Ability Hand joint targets (13-D: 7 arm + 6 hand); not in the release

other: per-taxel 6-axis IMU (BHI360) on each sensor PCB; quaternions logged by the ROS2 node but not released
retargeted robot joint positions (7 Franka + 6 Ability Hand) in the paper's training set, not released

sources: Google Drive files mags_public.pkl, rgbs_public.pkl, left_ir_public.pkl, right_ir_public.pkl (downloaded and read)
unconfirmed: hours = 2 and episodes = 140 are the paper's 'approximately two hours' and the project page's '140 demos'; the full set is not released, so neither was checked.
Released sample: 211 frames per stream (counted in all four pickles); 8.41 s from the first to last mags timestamp; mean step 40.07 ms (24.3-55.7 ms).
Sample recorded 2025-09-11 (UTC), derived from the mags timestamps (ns since Unix epoch).
fps 25 for the cameras is the ROS2 publish/logging rate (timer 0.04 s in realsense_node.py, paper 'logged as ROS2 bag files at 25 Hz'); the sensor stream itself is configured at 30 fps.
sensor rate_hz 25: firmware sets the BHI360 magnetometer virtual sensors to 25 Hz (glove.c) and the ROS2 node publishes synced packets every 0.04 s.

Unit: the paper and project page say raw magnetic flux in uT; the firmware forwards the BHI360 virtual-sensor int16 values without scaling. All released values are integers (z about -4,900 to -5,260).

mag0/mag1 per fingertip are the BHI360 'MAG_ID' stream and the 'MAG_PASS_META' stream of the same sensor board (sensor ids n and n+20 in bowie_node_synced.py); the paper describes two BMM350 magnetometers per PCB.
depth=false: the capture node also publishes aligned depth (16UC1), but it is not in the release; the paper computes depth offline from the IR pair.

scenes=1 derived from 'policies deployed in the same environment used to collect the human demonstrations'; scene_types 'lab' derived from the demonstrations being inside the robot's reachable workspace (Franka base visible in the RGB frames).
Task label 'wiping a stencilled marker pattern off a whiteboard with a sponge' combines the paper's task description with the RGB frames of the sample.
Whether palm taxels were recorded in the 140 demonstrations is not stated; the paper omits the palm for this task.
subjects and objects are not stated (the sample shows one gloved right hand, a sponge and a whiteboard).
'principle: magnetic' is the catalog category; the paper says magnetometers (BMM350) under a magnetized elastomer.
The project page's JSON-LD metadata carries "license": "https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT" for the page (ScholarlyArticle record) and the arXiv paper is CC BY 4.0; neither is stated for the data.

license.name: not stated
license.note: No sentence about data licensing or redistribution exists in data/README.md, the repository README, the project page text or the paper. The repository has no LICENSE file (GitHub API license: null); hardware/ros2/bowie_ros2_ws/bowie_ros/package.xml has '<license>TODO: License declaration</license>'. The project page's JSON-LD block lists "license": "https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT" as page metadata only; the arXiv paper is CC BY 4.0. Third-party firmware drivers in the repo carry their own licenses (ST, Bosch BHY2, FreeRTOS), not relevant to the data.

download.format: Four Python pickle files, each a list of 211 time-aligned items (aligned by list index): rgbs_public.pkl (protocol 4, numpy uint8 arrays via numpy.core.multiarray._reconstruct), left_ir_public.pkl and right_ir_public.pkl (protocol 5, numpy._core.numeric._frombuffer), mags_public.pkl (protocol 4, plain Python tuples (int timestamp_ns, list of 30 floats), no globals)
download.partial_fetch: Files download from https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=<file id>&export=download&confirm=t (no login; the three large files show a virus-scan page without confirm=t). HTTP Range requests return 206, and the IR pickles have a fixed 921,638 B stride per frame, so single frames can be range-read; mags_public.pkl is 60 KB. File ids: mags 1HbItKCHGw7IqF3jaMSK06-K0zLcfMJ14, rgbs 1OONLF0aPixpwPJWMrTNXMabtYz2lyoFI, left_ir 1Ha09vxpKm_h4Qi-iM1D9DuGEJiGB6sBE, right_ir 1-IB4oDPBPhcsN0WuQIBRgY8uFRBdHzuj.
download.local_copy: ~/data/ext/osmo/00/ (all four files; sha256 mags f134a72c..., rgbs 8c407c19..., left_ir e741d65a..., right_ir 88b6e9bc...)

channels.name: mags_public[i][1]
channels.unit: uT as stated by the paper (raw magnetic flux); firmware forwards BHI360 int16 values unscaled; all values are integers
channels.frame: each magnetometer's own sensor axes (x, y, z); orientation on the fingertip not documented
channels.note: Order per data/README.md and bowie_node_synced.py: index, middle, ring, pinky, thumb; per finger mag0 then mag1; per magnetometer x, y, z. Fingertip taxels only. Not calibrated force: the paper subtracts mag0 - mag1 per taxel (differential sensing) before the policy encoder. Observed: z about -4,900 to -5,260 on every magnetometer; x/y vary by up to ~1,100 within the clip. Differential |mag0 - mag1| deviates from the first-10-frame rest by 320-970 on all five fingertips between about 2 s and 7 s (contact with the sponge). Rest values differ per magnetometer (offsets not removed). 1-9% of consecutive samples repeat exactly (25 Hz sync of the latest buffered reading). Shown in the viewer as 3-axis vectors per fingertip.

channels.name: mags_public[i][0]
channels.note: ROS2 bag receive time of the /bowie/synced message (convert_bag_to_pkl.py). The only timestamps in the release; the image lists carry none and are aligned to it by index. Per-sensor firmware timestamps were dropped.

sample.reason: Data are downloadable without login (public Google Drive folder, HTTP range requests work). No license or terms for the data exist (data/README.md, repository README, project page text and paper are silent; no LICENSE file; package.xml says 'TODO: License declaration'), so redistribution is not forbidden: re-host and label the collection "License not stated". The project page's MIT JSON-LD tag and the paper's CC BY 4.0 do not cover the data and must not be shown as the data license.

episodes.task: wiping a stencilled marker pattern off a whiteboard with a sponge (right hand)
episodes.scene: robot workspace table with a whiteboard, one static RealSense D435
episodes.why: The only released episode. All 30 fingertip channels present (211 x 30, no NaN, no all-zero or constant channel; every channel takes 6-157 distinct integer values). Contact on all 5 fingertips: |(mag0 - mag1) - rest| (rest = mean of the first 10 frames, noise <= 6 counts) exceeds 100 counts for 2.0-6.3 s on index, middle and pinky, 2.0-6.8 s on ring and 2.3-6.2 s on thumb (75-113 frames each, peaks 967/623/798/388/322 for index/middle/ring/pinky/thumb). Whole clip kept: it is shorter than 10 s, so no window applies.

sample.fetch_estimate: 0 MB more: the whole release (972,374,859 B, four pickles) is already in ~/data/ext/osmo/00/. Re-hosted media estimated at a few MB: one 8.4 s RGB video (H.264, downscaled from 1280x720) and optionally the masked left IR video; episode JSON well under 2 MB (211 frames x 30 values).
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 1 task in the release (<= 6), so all taken. Episodes: the release holds exactly 1 episode, so the minimum of 3 episodes and the 2-3 per task rule cannot be met; 1 sampled. Length: 8.41 s is below the 10 s minimum and cannot be lengthened; kept whole (window null) because it is the only data released. Channels: all 30 released tactile values checked (palm taxels are not released, not missing from the episode). Contact: > 1 s above rest on all 5 fingertips. Budget: far below 2 MB JSON / ~30 MB media / ~20 GB download.
deviations: 1 episode instead of at least 3: the release contains a single demonstration.
8.41 s instead of 10-60 s: the only released demonstration is that long.

checks.method: mags_public.pkl read with a restricted unpickler (find_class blocked; the file holds only ints, floats, tuples and lists)
checks.z_channels_note: the z axis of each magnetometer varies only 5-111 counts over the clip (mag0 z: 5-10 counts); x/y carry the contact signal. Not stuck: 6-37 distinct values per z channel.

visualization.detail: Per fingertip taxel the differential signal (mag0 - mag1, as the paper's policy input) minus its rest value (mean of the first 10 frames): one cell per fingertip coloured by |deviation| (scale 0-1000), (x, y) arrow + z ring (full block 500), plots of the differential x, y, z per finger; all 30 raw channels as 5 per-finger plots (mag0 solid, mag1 dashed, x/y/z, each minus its own rest value). Cells placed after the paper's Fig. 5A taxel map (right hand, palm side, thumb on the right).

visualization.reason: ROS2 receive timestamps, not touch; used to check the uniform 25 Hz clock (max deviation 17 ms, spacing 24-56 ms) and stated in notes
